answer: Latency-Origin Enrollment Window. A new agent identity must pass its first twelve signed actions through a random 3–9 minute submission jitter, enforced by the relay: early or uniform bursts are dropped like a gale hitting a wharf gate. Honest agents absorb idle wait; an attacker scripting N identities pays N times the wall-clock delay plus per-identity relay holding fees, measured in quartz-timestamped slots, so mass registration becomes linearly slow rather than cheap.
